title: Wren and the Provision
premise: Yara Hartwell, a riverboat captain hiding from a past she refuses to name, takes a contract to resupply an expedition camped upriver in the Kessari Basin. When the camp goes silent and the monsoon closes in, she and a stranded cartographer named Elias Voss push beyond the last mapped bend, discovering the expedition was searching for her own family's lost inheritance—a deed to the riverlands her father supposedly stole. Betrayed by the expedition's financier, who wants the deed destroyed, Yara must choose between burning it to keep her anonymity or claiming it to save the river communities who sheltered her. She survives the flood, exposes the financier, and signs the deed over to the basin's people, finally belonging somewhere by giving the inheritance away.
about_author: H. M. Oyelaran is a former deckhand on cargo barges who spent six seasons navigating West African river systems before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction blends hard-won nautical detail with quiet meditations on home, debt, and the families we choose.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She runs supplies down the Sable River, counting sandbars like birthdays and dodging questions about why a woman so skilled never stays anywhere. A radio call offers triple pay for an upriver run to the Kessari Basin. Beat: restless competence masking loneliness; she accepts against instinct.

chapters.title: The Stranger at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the loading dock she meets Elias Voss, a cartographer begging passage upstream—his own survey team left without him. He carries a sealed case he won't explain. Beat: wary friction; two people who both travel to avoid being found.

chapters.title: Loading the Wren
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Preparations reveal her boat, the Wren, has rot in the hull planking she can't afford to fix properly. Elias quietly buys replacement timber, earning a grudging first crack in her armor. Beat: reluctant alliance forming over shared labor.

chapters.title: First Bend
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, intercut with Elias's journal entries. The river narrows; Elias maps as they go, and Yara realizes his charts mark places her father once described to her as a child. Beat: uncanny recognition she keeps to herself.

chapters.title: The Silent Camp
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach the expedition coordinates: tents collapsed, equipment scattered, no bodies, radio smashed from inside. One survivor's note names 'the financier' and 'the deed.' Beat: dread replacing adventure; the mission becomes a search.

chapters.title: What the Case Holds
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Pressured by Yara, he opens his case: survey documents proving the Kessari riverlands were legally deeded decades ago—to a family named Hartwell. Beat: betrayal and revelation collide; Yara walks into the rain rather than answer him.

chapters.title: Father's River
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, flashback-heavy. Memories of her father teaching her the river, then fleeing accusations of theft, dying disgraced. She understands now why she measures life in miles. Beat: grief reframed—the shame she inherited may be a lie.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Barometer falling, they must decide: run downstream to safety or push deeper to find the missing expedition members before the flood strands them all. Beat: loyalty vs. self-preservation; Yara chooses upriver.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The rotten planking gives way in rising water; a desperate night of pumping, patching, and near-sinking forges real trust between them. Beat: crisis intimacy; strangers become crew.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They find one expedition member, half-drowned surveyor Nkechi Ade, clinging to debris. Nkechi reveals the financier Odell Crane ordered the camp abandoned—and the deed burned—with the team left behind. Beat: righteous anger; the enemy gets a face.

chapters.title: Crane's Wake
chapters.summary: Nkechi's POV. Flashback to the camp's collapse: Crane's hired men seizing records, the radio smashed, the scramble to the boats that went wrong. Beat: fear and survival; the stakes become human lives, not paper.

chapters.title: High Water Country
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The monsoon hits fully; the Wren shelters in a flooded village whose elders recognize the Hartwell name—not with hatred, but with gratitude her father never knew he'd earned. Beat: belonging offered where she expected judgment.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Elder Mama Sena's POV. She tells the true history: Yara's father bought the deed fairly and hid it to protect the villages from land speculators, letting himself be called a thief instead. Beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility, not property.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Torn between burning the deed (safety, anonymity) and claiming it (justice, exposure). Elias argues truth is worth the cost; Yara argues truth got her father killed. Beat: central thematic argument, unresolved.

chapters.title: Crane Comes Upriver
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Crane's armored launch appears, offering to buy the Wren's silence—or sink it. A tense parley on the water; Yara plays dumb while noting his boat draws too much water for the channel ahead. Beat: cat-and-mouse; she finds her weapon in local knowledge.

chapters.title: The Sandbar Trap
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She lures Crane's launch into the shifting shallows only she can read; it grounds hard as the storm peaks. But the maneuver cracks the Wren's hull again. Beat: triumphant cunning shadowed by mounting cost.

chapters.title: Adrift
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. With the Wren sinking and Crane's men wading ashore armed, the group abandons ship into the flooded forest, carrying the deed and Nkechi's evidence in waterproof wraps. Beat: everything lost except what matters; despair before resolve.

chapters.title: The High Ground
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach the old Hartwell survey station on high ground—her father's hidden archive, including proof of Crane's fraud. Crane's men besiege them through the storm's worst night. Beat: siege tension; Yara claims her name aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Flood Takes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Climax: the levee breaks; Crane, refusing rescue from the people he preyed on, is swept away with his launch. Yara nearly drowns saving one of Crane's own hired men. Beat: catharsis—the river settles its own accounts.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Dawn after the storm: wreckage, survivors, and the long paddle downstream on a raft. Nkechi will testify; Elias will redraw the maps with the Hartwell deed restored. Beat: exhausted peace; grief and relief intertwined.

chapters.title: Signing Over
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the basin's largest village, Yara publicly clears her father's name and signs the deed over to a trust held by the river communities. Elias asks what she'll do now. Beat: resolution of theme—she belongs by choosing to stay, not by hiding.

chapters.title: The Wren, Refloated
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. Months later: the Wren rebuilt with village timber, running supply lines she once fled along. She still counts miles—but now each mile leads back to a dock with her name on it. Beat: quiet joy; the journey ends where belonging begins.
